sections.h2: How do I sell my house fast in Union City, GA?
sections.html:
Most Union City owners choose between a traditional agent listing, a for-sale-by-owner sale, or a direct purchase by a cash buyer. A cash buyer is the quickest path when the house needs work, carries a tax balance, or is tenant occupied.

Union City is in southern Fulton County, so the paperwork you will meet runs through Fulton offices and the city's Community Development and Finance departments. Settling those items first shortens almost any sale.

  • Pull your deed and mortgage payoff statement.
  • Confirm there are no open building permits or code citations on the address.
  • Check that city and county property taxes are current.
  • Gather HOA documents if the street has covenants.

A buyer paying cash will usually offer less than a fully repaired listing, and the trade is certainty and speed for price. Compare the net you would keep after repairs, carrying costs and agent commission before you decide.

sections.h2: What kind of city is Union City, and why does it matter to sellers?
sections.html:
Union City describes itself as a small city in the southern part of Fulton County, about fifteen minutes from Atlanta and ten miles from Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport. That airport distance is a selling point for buyers who commute or travel often.

The city also lists several designations, including Camera Ready City, with Atlanta Metro Studios named as one of the region's large production facilities. The Census also lists transportation and warehousing receipts of $439,256 thousand for 2022 in Union City.

Census figures show steady growth: 19,456 residents in the 2010 census, 26,830 in the 2020 census and an estimate of 29,910 for July 1, 2025. Land area is 19.67 square miles in the 2020 count, so the city has grown by adding households inside a mostly fixed footprint.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show for Union City homes?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counts 40.4 percent of Union City homes as owner occupied, so rental houses make up a large share of the market. Figures are the 2020 to 2024 survey estimates unless marked.

sections.h2: How are Union City property taxes billed?
sections.html:
Union City taxes now appear on the Fulton County property tax bill. The city's Finance page states that the 2026 millage rate is 11.296, made up of 11.132 for maintenance and operations and 0.164 for bonds.

The city says existing homestead, disability, disabled veteran and senior exemptions on city taxes stay in place without a new application, and that new Senior Homestead applications go to Fulton County directly. Delinquent city taxes for 2024 and earlier years are still collected by Union City and remain subject to interest, penalties and tax sale proceedings.

The same page divides the work between two Fulton offices. The Board of Assessors maintains ownership, mailing addresses, valuation, homestead applications and appeals. The Tax Commissioner creates the bill and collects the payment.

  • Fulton County Tax Commissioner: 404-613-6100
  • Fulton County Board of Assessors: 404-612-6440

If a prior-year city balance exists on your parcel, clear it before closing because a buyer's lender or title agent will find it.

sections.h2: How does a Fulton County assessment appeal work for a Union City owner?
sections.html:
Fulton owners can appeal within 45 days of the date on the Notice of Assessment. The 2026 notices went online June 19, 2026, and the county gave Friday, July 31, 2026 as the deadline for most owners unless another date is printed on the notice, so that window has closed for this cycle.

You can appeal only the assessed value, not the estimated tax. Appeals may be filed online through the county assessor site, in person or by mail, and you choose among a Board of Equalization hearing, non-binding arbitration on value, or a Hearing Officer, with fees possible for the last two. The process can take months, and a temporary tax bill may arrive while the appeal is pending, which you must pay to avoid penalties.

The Board of Assessors has a South Fulton Service Center at 5600 Stonewall Tell Road, Suite 224, and you can call 404-612-6440. The county notes that April 1 is the standard homestead deadline, with a second window during the appeal period for owners who qualified as of January 1.

sections.h2: What city permits and code rules apply when selling in Union City?
sections.html:
Union City requires a building permit for most construction work, and work can start only after the permit is issued. A permit expires if construction does not begin within 180 days or if it is suspended for more than 180 consecutive days.

Permit applications, plan submittals, invoice payment and inspection scheduling run through the city's IWORQ online portal. Inspection requests need the permit number and contractor code, and requests for next-business-day inspection must come in before 4:00 pm Eastern. The Community Development office is at 5041 Union St, open Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, and permit questions go to 770-515-7950, option 1.

Code Enforcement accepts violations by phone, fax, email or area survey, and an officer investigates within 24 hours of a report. Its phone line is (770) 515-7890, Monday through Friday, 7:00 AM to 4:00 PM. Officers inspecting one property may also survey adjacent properties for violations, so a neighbor's complaint can lead to a look at your yard.

The Planning Division posts the current zoning ordinance, development regulations and subdivision regulations, along with the Comprehensive Plan and Future Land Use Map. Check the zoning for your parcel if you expect a buyer to use the house in a particular way.

sections.h2: What are the closing and recording steps for a Union City sale?
sections.html:
The deed is recorded with the Fulton County Clerk of Superior Court after the real estate transfer tax is paid. The state's rate is $1 for the first $1,000 of the sale price and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part of $100.

Georgia law makes the seller liable for the tax, and a contract can assign it to the buyer. The PT-61 transfer tax form is filed online through the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority, with one form per deed.

Union City students are served by Fulton County Schools. The district's South Learning Center is at 4025 Flat Shoals Road in Union City, and the district publishes an address lookup that shows the elementary, middle and high school zones for any home, which is useful to include when a buyer asks.

faqs.q: Who bills property tax in Union City?
faqs.a: Fulton County sends one bill that includes the city portion. Union City's Finance page lists 2026 city millage as 11.296 and says earlier delinquent balances, for 2024 and prior years, are still collected by the city.

faqs.q: Does Union City have to inspect my house before I sell it?
faqs.a: The city's permit pages do not list a sale inspection. They do require permits for most construction, and inspections are scheduled through the online portal, so confirm that past work on your house was permitted and signed off before a buyer asks.

faqs.q: What if my Fulton assessment appeal deadline has passed?
faqs.a: You lose the right to appeal that year's value once the printed deadline passes. For 2026 the county gave July 31 for most owners. Watch the date on next year's notice and file early, online or at a Board of Assessors office.

faqs.q: Can I report a neighboring code problem before I list my house?
faqs.a: Yes. Union City accepts reports by phone at (770) 515-7890, fax, email or an area survey during an inspection, and says an officer investigates within 24 hours. Reporting early can clear an eyesore before buyers visit.

faqs.q: Which school district covers Union City homes?
faqs.a: Fulton County Schools covers the city, and the district's South Learning Center is on Flat Shoals Road in Union City. Use the district's address lookup to confirm the elementary, middle and high school zones for your house.
